Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the reply from the visitors to 278 from the home side. Azan Awais has walked out with a new opening pair in Abdullah Fazal. Taskin Ahmed is ready to bowl the first over for Bangladesh. Away we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Shahzad shines for Pakistan - Mohammad Abbas and Khurram Shahzad were certainly the pick of the bowlers for Pakistan. Abbas got early breakthroughs, picking up 3 of the first 4 wickets. After which, Shahzad got in the mix and made it three wickets for himself. However, someone like a Hasan Ali couldn't maintain pressure when he got the ball as Sajid Khan toiled long and hard from the other end. Shahzad finished with a four-fer as Ali came back late to grab the last two wickets. Right then, will about half an hour left in the day's play, it will be a tricky period for the Pakistan batters and the Bangladeshi bowlers will be eager to make early inroads. Stay tuned as Pakistan's first innings is up next.

Das the differentiating factor - Bangladesh huffed and puffed their way to 116/6 ass four out of their top five batters all got into the 20s and got out. Litton Das the cams in and was their shining light light, stitching a few meaningful stands with the lower order. He went on to score a beautiful century, his 6th in Test cricket and almost took his side to a total of 300 runs.

A hard-fought first innings comes to an end - A couple of quick breakthroughs to finish off the first innings, but Bangladesh have done a decent job to get to a respectable total of 278 runs. Overall, Pakistan will still be the happier of the two teams, having bowled out the hosts on Day 1.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to Sylhet! We are all set for the post-Tea session to get underway on Day 1. The umpires are back out in the middle, and Litton Das and Taijul Islam are back as well, ready to resume their stay at the crease. Also, Mohammad Abbas is back and will start off the new session, just as he did post-Lunch. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Pacers rule the roost for Pakistan - Mohammad Abbas was already prolific in the first session, but he started off the post-Lunch session even better. He bowled a maiden to start proceedings and soon enough, there was enough pressure built that he managed to get rid of the opposition skipper. Khurram Shahzad then replaced Abbas in the attack and picked up a couple of quick wickets, making it three apiece for him and Abbas. Sajid Khan held up one end really well and bowled throughout the session, without any breaks. However, once Abbas and Shahzad finished their spells, Hasan Ali and Sajid failed to build any sort of pressure on the batters, allowing a stand to flourish. With that said, Pakistan are still in a solid position and a wicket or two right after Tea, could still see Bangladesh get bowled out for under 200 runs, which could be a massive deal in this Test match. Do join us for the final session on Day 1 at 9 am GMT.

Lots of starts, no big knocks - Such has been the story for Bangladesh that 4 of their top 5 batters got into the 20s, but failed to make the most of a start. Having lost 3 wickets in the first session, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim, two experienced statesmen, looked to build a stand, but they were a bit too sluggish at the start of the second session and that allowed Pakistan to take advantage. They went from 106/3 to 116/6 in a matter of a few overs, but then Litton Das came in and launched a smart counter-attack, managing to hog the strike for most of the deliveries and Taijul Islam seemed decently assured with the bat to take the hosts from 116/6 to 168/6 by the end of the session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28 overs, 67 runs, and 3 wickets. It will be a session that will count as positive for Pakistan, but they will feel that by now, Bangladesh should have been bundled out. Litton Das has batted very smartly, and Taijul Islam has given him excellent support to wrestle a bit of momentum back fo the hosts.

Bowling analysis and injury concerns - Pakistan's bowling attack started with immense discipline, but their rhythm was temporarily disrupted by Bangladesh's early, aggressive approach. Mohammad Abbas looked consistent throughout the morning session to pick up two crucial wickets, while Khurram Shahzad earned one for his efforts. The major concern for the visitors remains a serious injury to Hasan Ali, who had to be stretchered off the field after absorbing a sharp blow to the head. Imam-ul-Haq stepped in as the substitute fielder, but Ali was back on the field after some rest and restarted his spell. We will be back with live coverage of the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT.

Double blow and stabilizing resurgence - Just as the Bangladeshi batsmen seemed comfortable and began transitioning into a more defensive mindset, Pakistan broke through the burgeoning partnership. It was once again Mohammad Abbas who provided the crucial breakthrough by dismissing the dangerous Tanzid, and Mominul followed him back to the pavilion shortly after, dismissed by Khurram Shahzad, leaving Bangladesh in a spot of bother. Despite the quick double-strike, senior batsmen Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim steadied the ship. The experienced duo constructed an unbeaten 38-run partnership, safely navigating the remaining overs to guide Bangladesh to the Lunch break without further damage.

Early disasters and explosive counterattack - Pakistan capitalized on the overcast conditions and a green pitch immediately after asking Bangladesh to bat. Opening bowler Mohammad Abbas made an instant impact by removing Mahmudul Hasan Joy for a duck on the very second ball of the match. However, the early setback did not deter the home side. Debutant Tanzid Hasan took charge with an aggressively counter-attacking approach, smashing a flurry of boundaries to shift the pressure right back onto the Pakistani bowlers. Senior batter Mominul Haque supported the debutant brilliantly, rotating the strike effectively and keeping the scoreboard ticking at a brisk pace.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start this riveting contest! The two umpires have already taken their positions just after the national anthems. The players of Pakistan have scattered and Mohammad Abbas is walking towards his bowling mark with the red cherry in his hands. For Bangladesh, it's Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Tanzid Hasan to open the innings. Hassan Joy to take the strike. Abbas will go with three slips and a gully. Away we go...

Captain of Bangladesh - Najmul Hossain Shanto says that he would have bowled first as well. Shanto underscores a firm commitment to winning rather than playing for a draw, noting that the squad always aims for victory on home soil through consistent performances and daily execution of high-quality cricket. Finally, Shanto confirms two changes to the lineup, announcing that Tanzid Tamim makes his debut due to an unfortunate injury to Shadman, while Shoriful replaces Ebadot in the playing XI.

Skipper of Pakistan - Shan Masood opts to bowl first after observing grass on the pitch, noting that recent weather has kept the surface under covers and remains unpredictable for the coming days. Shan adds that the decision aligns with the strategic necessity of taking 20 wickets in Test cricket to secure a victory. Masood confirms three changes to the playing XI, bringing Babar, Sajid Khan, and Khurram into the side for Imam, Noman, and Shaheen respectively. Reflecting on the team's recovery from their previous match, Shan stresses the importance of mental and physical fitness alongside learning from past mistakes. Ultimately, he highlights that every fixture carries immense weight in the World Test Championship, urging his team to focus on the present, deliver a strong opening day, and build a commanding position.

PITCH REPORT - Athar Ali Khan is pitchside with his valuable insights. He starts off saying that the groundmen have done a solid job as it's been raining for the past few weeks in Sylhet. Khan says the wicket's a bit damp, less green than Mirpur. With rain and moisture, there's something for pacers, and spinners might get help too. He thinks that the team winning the toss will bowl first, teams batting first have won thrice. Both captains will likely bowl first, given the weather's uncertainty.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Azan Awais, Shan Masood (C), Babar Azam (In place of Imam-ul-Haq), Abdullah Fazal, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan( WK), Salman Agha, Khurram Shahzad (In place of Noman Ali), Sajid Khan (In place of Shaheen Afridi), Hasan Ali, Mohammad Abbas.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Tanzid Hasan (On Test debut, in for Shadman Islam), Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taijul Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam (In place of Ebadot Hossain) and Nahid Rana.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the coin flip and they will be BOWLING first.

Tactical maneuvers amidst overcast skies - Varying elements and local pitch behaviors are set to heavily influence team strategies over the coming days. While the Sylhet pitch typically offers reliable turn for spin bowlers, an initial layer of grass could provide early joy for the seamers. But folks, the forecast is unfortunately not looking favorable for a full day of cricket, with a significant chance of rain. That said, let's keep our fingers crossed and hope for the best!

Pakistan's rescue mission and star reinforcement - The tourists arrive in Sylhet under extreme duress, needing a radical overhaul of their batting approach to preserve their pride. Pakistan's top order capitulated easily against high-quality spin in Dhaka, exposing critical technical flaws. To square the series, their batsmen must display tighter defensive discipline and construct long, resilient partnerships. Fortunately, the visitor's camp has received a major morale injection with Babar Azam certified fit for selection. Having recovered from a left knee injury that sidelined him previously, his return injects immense stability and world-class experience into a shaken batting order.

Bangladesh's formula of total dominance - The home team displayed phenomenal grit, composure, and tactical brilliance throughout the first Test. Bangladesh dictated terms early by manufacturing a colossal first-innings total that deflated the opposition. Their deep batting order absorbed pressure effortlessly, while their bowling unit consistently snuffed out Pakistani fightbacks during key sessions. The final day belonged entirely to the Tigers' fiery bowling artillery. Speedster Nahid Rana dismantled the visitor's lower order with a relentless five-wicket burst. This lethal spell dismantled Pakistan's defense, securing a historic 104-run triumph and handing the hosts total psychological ascendancy.

Battle lines drawn in Sylhet - Cricket enthusiasts worldwide are warmly welcomed to the Pakistan tour of Bangladesh. An electric atmosphere envelops the scenic Sylhet International Cricket Stadium as Day 1 of the pivotal second Test gets underway. The hosts, Bangladesh, hold a decisive 1-0 lead in this brief two-match window. They put forth a clinical display in Dhaka to claim the series opener. With vital ICC World Test Championship points at stake, this final fixture shall be a cracker as well. The tension is palpable as both camps prepare to lock horns on the field.
